title: On‑Prem Kubernetes hybrid bootstrap (iPXE + vSphere) — terraform notes and upgrade checklist
content:
Purpose and scope:
This is a working playbook + notes for bootstrapping hybrid on‑prem Kubernetes clusters that use both bare‑metal (iPXE + container host) nodes and vSphere VM workers/control plane. Goal: repeatable terraform flows, minimal manual steps in the data center, and an upgrade path that safely handles mixed‑lifecycle nodes.

Intended audience:
- Platform Engineers doing cluster provisioning at customer sites
- Solutions Eng when designing private deployment packages
- SREs responsible for upgrades and runbooks

High level approach / constraints:
- Use terraform to orchestrate everything we can: DHCP/iPXE configs, DNS entries, vSphere VMs, IPAM assignments, and bootstrap artifacts (cloud‑init, ignition-like user data).
- Bare metal machines provision via iPXE PXE boot + a small provisioning image that pulls a host.ini from our artifact S3 (signed).
- We use kubeadm for control plane bootstrapping for deterministic control over certs and upgrade workflow.
- State backend: remote S3 (or object store) + Dynamo/Consul for locks depending on customer environment.
- Must support staged network installs (airgapped / low egress) using pre-seeded images and local registry mirror.

Architecture summary (textual):
- Bootstrap host (laptop / bootstrap VM) runs terraform apply which:
  * Uploads artifacts (kubeadm config, bootstrap scripts) to customer artifact repo (S3/minio)
  * Registers DHCP/iPXE entries for baremetal nodes with MAC -> image mapping
  * Creates vSphere control plane VMs if required (template -> clone -> power on)
  * Creates DNS A records and SRV entries for control plane LB / api-server
  * Generates kubeadm init configuration with local CA (optionally KMS/HSM backing)
  * Waits for nodes to join and applies CNI/storage operators

Pre-req checklist (quick):
- IP plan and VLANs documented + available
- DHCP scope that supports iPXE booting and can be updated by terraform (or manually coordinated)
- vSphere credentials and template image present and network tags verified
- Artifact store credentials and URL (S3 compatible)
- SSH jump host for initial debug
- kubeadm binary pinned and archived for offline installs if needed

iPXE bare‑metal flow (notes):
- Using iPXE chain to an http-served provisioning image (initramfs+vmlinuz) that runs our small installer.
- Installer pulls host metadata from /artifacts/hosts/${mac}.json. That JSON contains: role (controlplane/worker), kubelet flags, kubeadm token, DNS, NTP.
- Terraform module (module.ipxe) must output MAC -> iPXE entry id, so we can later clear entries on decommission.
- Recommended: use signed host metadata and verify via gpg public key shipped in initramfs.

Terraform module notes (rough):
- modules/ipxe (new): variables: dhcp_api_url, artifacts_bucket, hosts_map (map of mac -> role), mac_to_ip (optional). outputs: entry_ids (map), boot_script_url (string).
- modules/vsphere-k8s: variables: template_name, datacenter, network_ids, disk_policy, vm_tags, kube_role (controlplane/worker). outputs: vm_ips, vm_ids.
- modules/cluster (wrapper): accepts cluster_name, cidr_pools, control_plane_count (n), worker_pools (list of maps), ipxe_hosts (list). It invokes ipxe + vsphere modules and writes out a rendered kubeadm config to artifacts.
- State recommended: use a workspace per cluster and remote state per customer. Use read_only policies for infra operators where possible.
- Idempotency: embed a 10m backoff loop into tf apply scripts to handle DHCP propagation delays (DHCP API eventual consistency is our typical pain point).
- Secrets: do not store kubeadm bootstrap tokens in plain tf state. Use vault provider to inject ephemeral join tokens right after kubeadm init and remove them from state.

Example terraform snippet (text only):
- brief example we keep in the module README (HCL excerpt):
  module "ipxe" {
    source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//ipxe?ref=main"
    dhcp_api_url = var.dhcp_api_url
    artifacts_bucket = var.artifacts_bucket
    hosts_map = var.ipxe_hosts
  }

  module "vsphere" {
    source = "git::https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules.git//vsphere-k8s?ref=v1.3.0"
    template_name = var.vsphere_template
    count = var.vsphere_workers_count
  }

Bootstrapping sequence (detailed steps):
1) terraform apply (artifacts only) -> uploads kubeadm templates, node userdata, registry mirror list.
2) terraform apply (ipxe + vsphere) -> create VMs + ipxe entries.
3) For control plane on bare metal: node boots -> runs installer -> kubeadm init --config /etc/kubeadm/init.yaml -> copies /etc/kubernetes/admin.conf to artifact store (encrypted) and posts join token to vault.
4) For vSphere control plane: after VM is up we run remote command (ssh) to start kubeadm with same config.
5) Apply CNI (we prefer Cilium for its eBPF performance but support Calico in sites that need NetworkPolicy compat).
6) Install storage operator (Rook Ceph for bare metal sites, vSphere CSI + CNS for vSphere dominant sites).
7) Label nodes and taint control-plane appropriately; run smoke tests (DNS, kube-dns, kubelet health, sample app).

Node registration caveats:
- When mixing bare metal and vSphere control plane nodes, ensure control-plane components are scheduled with nodeSelector to avoid scheduler confusion during early boot (some kubelets register faster than others).
- Use kubeadm control-plane-endpoint with an L4 LB (keepalived or external lb) that terraform configures as a VIP.

Upgrade plan (safe path for mixed clusters):
- Strategy: control plane first, one node at a time, then workers in waves by pool. Do not do global CNI upgrade with cluster going across major versions.
- Pre-upgrade checks: api-server latency, etcd health, available disk on control plane nodes, recent snapshots of etcd (stored in artifact store).
- Control plane upgrade steps: 
  * cordon + drain (if worker) -> for control plane use kubeadm upgrade apply on one node at a time, verify etcd member healthy and in quorum after each upgrade.
  * If kubeadm-managed control-plane, follow kubeadm upgrade docs: upgrade binaries, kubeadm upgrade plan, kubeadm upgrade apply, restart kubelet kube-proxy etc.
- Worker upgrade waves: annotate workers with pool=legacy/fast (based on kernel/kubelet ABI). Upgrade small percentage (5–10%) first as canary, run e2e smoke, then continue.
- Rollback: keep pre-upgrade etcd snapshot and the previous machine image in the artifact repo. In practice rollback is a full cluster restore — make sure we can restore etcd quickly (test quarterly).

Operational runbook snippets (commands):
- Drain worker: kubectl cordon <node>; kubectl drain <node> --ignore-daemonsets --delete-local-data --timeout=30m
- Uncordon: kubectl uncordon <node>
- Check etcd: ETCDCTL_API=3 etcdctl --endpoints=https://127.0.0.1:2379 --cacert=/etc/kubernetes/pki/etcd/ca.crt "member list"
- Snapshot etcd (backup): kubeadm alpha certs or etcdctl snapshot save /tmp/etcd-snap.db (copy to artifact store)

Testing and smoke checks post-bootstrap:
- kube-dns, core components running, kube-proxy ready
- deploy small busybox + curl cluster-local svc from worker => api responds
- metrics: token issuance, containerd version, kubelet logs for OOMs

Airgap specifics:
- preseed images and helm charts into local registry mirror. Terraform should be able to upload artifacts directly to the local registry bucket (S3 path).
- do not rely on cloud metadata services for token retrieval; bake tokens into signed host metadata and rotate on first boot.

Open questions / TODOs (very much WIP):
- Decide canonical artifact signing approach: sigstore vs GPG. Need to align with security team for attestation.
- Vault integration pattern for ephemeral join tokens needs standard library in terraform modules (currently ad‑hoc).
- Decide recommended CNI (Cilium) but document fallback config for Calico policy features some customers need.
- Add a terraform null_resource based transient ssh-runner for vSphere post‑provision steps so we have single invocation that waits for kubeadm join.

Known failure modes and mitigations:
- DHCP entry propagation delay -> build reapply loop and exponential backoff in ci pipeline.
- Mixed time sources -> NTP/chrony config enforced in bootstrap; failures cause kubelet certificate skew errors.
- Etcd quorum loss during control‑plane upgrades -> require snapshot + additional etcd member cold standby in the plan for clusters >3 nodes.

Appendix A — quick troubleshooting checklist (first 10m):
- Are VMs/servers powering on? Check IPMI / vSphere task logs.
- Is iPXE fetching the right URL? curl the boot script from the local http server.
- Did the node get an IP and route to artifact store? traceroute/artifact curl.
- kubelet refusing to register? Check kubelet config: --fail-swap-on and cgroup driver mismatches are common.

Appendix B — references:
- internal confluence: https://confluence.redwood/infra/onprem-hybrid-arch
- terraform modules repo: https://github.com/redwood-inference/terraform-modules
- jira epic: INFRA-2124

Notes to self: keep this doc light — push full reference content into module READMEs and a runbook in confluence. This file is the working quickplay for the next customer onsite (Oct 2025).
